key: O ye who believe! Be ye staunch in justice, witnesses for Allah, even though it be against yourselves or (your) parents or (your) kindred, whether (the case be of) a rich man or a poor man, for Allah is nearer unto both (them ye are).
s: After rulings on women and orphans, the believers are charged to bear true witness; al-Tabari, on 4:135, reads it as schooling them against the false vouching given for the Banu Ubayriq over their theft, so that no wealth, poverty or kinship bends a witness.

evidence.words: وهذه الآية عندي تأديبٌ من الله جل ثناؤه عبادَه المؤمنين أن يفعلوا ما فعله الذين عذَروا بني أبيرق= في سرقتهم ما سرقوا … ولا يحملنكم غِنَى من شهدتم له أو فقره أو قرابته ورَحِمُه منكم، على الشهادة له بالزور، ولا على ترك الشهادة عليه بالحق وكتمانها.
evidence.gloss: This ayah, in my view, is God’s schooling of His believing servants against doing what was done by those who excused the Banu Ubayriq in the theft they committed … Let not the wealth, the poverty, or the kinship and blood-tie to you of the one you testify for carry you to false witness for him, nor to leaving off true witness against him and concealing it.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, An-Nisa 4:135, at 627; first sentence of the unit). The reading is al-Tabari’s own: in the packet on 4:135, after glossing the ayah, Abu Jaʿfar says in his own voice (عندي) that it schools the believers against doing what those did who excused the Banu Ubayriq over their theft and testified to their good character, and that no wealth, poverty or kinship should carry a witness to false testimony or to concealing the truth; al-Suddi’s view that it was revealed on the Prophet judging between a rich and a poor man is reported as another view, and the sentence does not claim it. CORRECTED the plain sense only: the proposal opened ‘After a rebuke to those who pleaded for wrongdoers’, but that rebuke is 4:109, twenty-six ayahs back, with 4:127 to 4:134 (women, orphans, wives, God’s ownership of heaven and earth) between; tying 4:135 to the pleaders is al-Tabari’s reading carried into the plain sense. Now ‘After rulings on women and orphans, the believers are charged to bear true witness’, faithful to 4:127 to 4:130, no four-word run from the verse. Reading half, src and place unchanged. 44 words; entry-check ok.
